claim: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has evolved into one of the most effective structure determination tools in modern day structural biology, achieving in recent years resolutions rivalling those of X-ray crystallography or NMR spectroscopy.
source: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has evolved into one of the most effective structure determination tools in modern day structural biology, achieving in recent years resolutions rivalling those of X-ray crystallography or NMR spectroscopy (Cheng, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cheng, 2015, indicating this is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Cryo-EM based structure determination overcomes the arduous task of preparing well-ordered crystals of macromolecules.
source: Furthermore, cryo-EM based structure determination overcomes two major bottlenecks faced in traditional X-ray crystallography, namely, the arduous task of preparing well-ordered crystals of macromolecules (Unger, 2002), and the more fundamental problem with capturing these molecules in unphysiological states as a result of crystal contacts (Neutze et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Unger, 2002, indicating this is established knowledge.

claim: Cryo-EM overcomes the problem with capturing molecules in unphysiological states as a result of crystal contacts.
source: Furthermore, cryo-EM based structure determination overcomes two major bottlenecks faced in traditional X-ray crystallography, namely, the arduous task of preparing well-ordered crystals of macromolecules (Unger, 2002), and the more fundamental problem with capturing these molecules in unphysiological states as a result of crystal contacts (Neutze et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Neutze et al., 2015, indicating this is established knowledge.

claim: Cryo-EM provides a natural way of resolving the structures of large macromolecular complexes.
source: Consequently, cryo-EM provides a natural way of resolving the structures of large macromolecular complexes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the previously stated advantages of cryo-EM over crystallography.

claim: MDFF has proven to be an extremely successful refinement method as evidenced by its numerous applications.
source: MDFF, in particular, has proven to be an extremely successful refinement method as evidenced by its numerous applications (Goh et al., 2015; McGreevy et al., 2016) ranging from the intricate ribosomal machinery (Villa et al., 2009; Trabuco et al., 2011; Frauenfeld et al., 2011; Wickles et al., 2014) to a host of non-enveloped viruses (Zhao et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations documenting applications of MDFF.

claim: MDFF's success has been limited to structure determination from typically low-resolution cryo-EM maps in the 7–25 Å range.
source: So far this success has been limited to structure determination from typically low-resolution cryo-EM maps in the 7–25 Å range which, indeed, represented the state-of-the-art at the time of MDFF's inception (Trabuco et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Trabuco et al., 2008, indicating the historical context of MDFF development.

claim: Seminal advances in detection hardware and programs over the past three years have enabled the routine availability of high-resolution (<5 Å) EM maps.
source: However, seminal advances in detection hardware and programs over the past three years (Li et al., 2013; Milazzo et al., 2011) have enabled now the routine availability of high-resolution (<5 Å) EM maps for a range of biological systems including ion channels (Liao et al., 2013), enzymes (Bartesaghi et al., 2014, 2015), membrane fusion machinery (Zhao et al., 2015), and key functional components of the ribosome (Fischer et al., 2015; Brown et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations documenting advances in hardware and examples of high-resolution maps.

claim: High-resolution maps pose an imminent challenge to traditional map-guided structure determination methods.
source: High-resolution maps pose an imminent challenge to the traditional map-guided structure determination methods as the maps now characterize near-atomic scale features, the interpretation of which requires extremely precise structure building and validation protocols (DiMaio et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to DiMaio et al., 2015, indicating this is a recognized challenge in the field.

claim: Conformation of protein sidechains are now discernible within high-resolution maps and require precise modeling of dihedral angles up to Cβ atoms.
source: For example, conformation of the protein sidechains, which are more flexible than the backbone, are now discernible within the maps and, thus, require precise modeling of the dihedral angles up to Cβ atoms while also respecting the map boundaries (Barad et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Barad et al., 2015, indicating this is established knowledge about high-resolution map interpretation.

claim: Cascade MDFF and resolution exchange MDFF sequentially re-refine a search model against a series of maps of progressively higher resolutions.
source: Two structure determination methods, based on the molecular dynamics flexible fitting (MDFF) paradigm, are presented that resolve sub-5 Å cryo-electron microscopy (EM) maps with either single structures or ensembles of such structures. The methods, denoted cascade MDFF and resolution exchange MDFF, sequentially re-refine a search model against a series of maps of progressively higher resolutions, which ends with the original experimental resolution.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the methodology presented in the manuscript.

claim: Sequential re-refinement enables MDFF to achieve a radius of convergence of ~25 Å demonstrated with the accurate modeling of β-galactosidase and TRPV1 proteins at 3.2 Å and 3.4 Å resolution, respectively.
source: Application of sequential re-refinement enables MDFF to achieve a radius of convergence of ~25 Å demonstrated with the accurate modeling of β-galactosidase and TRPV1 proteins at 3.2 Å and 3.4 Å resolution, respectively.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: MDFF refinements offer map-model validation and B-factor determination criteria based on the inherent dynamics of the macromolecules studied, captured by means of local root mean square fluctuations.
source: The MDFF refinements uniquely offer map-model validation and B-factor determination criteria based on the inherent dynamics of the macromolecules studied, captured by means of local root mean square fluctuations.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data and analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The MDFF tools described are available to researchers through an easy-to-use and cost-effective cloud computing resource on Amazon Web Services.
source: The MDFF tools described are available to researchers through an easy-to-use and cost-effective cloud computing resource on Amazon Web Services.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the availability of the tools, supported by implementation details in the manuscript.

claim: Direct MDFF of the 3 Å synthetic map of carbon monoxide dehydrogenase performed for 2 ns converged to a structure with an RMSD of 7 Å relative to the target model.
source: Direct MDFF of the 3 Å synthetic map performed for 2 ns converged to a structure with an RMSD of 7 Å relative to the target model.
evidence: This is experimental data from the proof-of-principle computation.

claim: cMDFF-generated structures of carbon monoxide dehydrogenase are within 1.7 Å RMSD of the target.
source: In sharp contrast, the cMDFF- and ReMDFF-generated structures are within 1.7 Å and 1 Å RMSD of the target (see the inset of Figure 1).
evidence: This is experimental data from the proof-of-principle computation, with reference to Figure 1.

claim: ReMDFF-generated structures of carbon monoxide dehydrogenase are within 1 Å RMSD of the target.
source: In sharp contrast, the cMDFF- and ReMDFF-generated structures are within 1.7 Å and 1 Å RMSD of the target (see the inset of Figure 1).
evidence: This is experimental data from the proof-of-principle computation, with reference to Figure 1.

claim: The new protocols extend the radius of convergence to at least 7 Å.
source: The results demonstrate that the new protocols are capable of attaining well-fit structures where direct MDFF does not. In particular, one can think of the new protocols as extending the radius of convergence to at least 7 Å, rendering the fitting procedures less dependent on the quality of the starting structure.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing successful fitting from a 7 Å RMSD starting structure.

claim: RMSD of the cMDFF-fitted β-galactosidase structure with respect to the reported de novo model is 0.7 Å.
source: Summarized in Table 1, the fitting results, in terms of quality of fit as well as model quality, are significantly better for cMDFF and ReMDFF than for direct MDFF: (i) RMSD of the fitted structure with respect to the reported de novo model is 0.7 Å and 0.9 Å for cMDFF and ReMDFF respectively, much lower than the 3.7 Å RMSD attained with direct MDFF (Figure 2—figure supplement 3a)
evidence: This is experimental data from the β-galactosidase refinement, presented in Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 3a.

claim: RMSD of the ReMDFF-fitted β-galactosidase structure with respect to the reported de novo model is 0.9 Å.
source: Summarized in Table 1, the fitting results, in terms of quality of fit as well as model quality, are significantly better for cMDFF and ReMDFF than for direct MDFF: (i) RMSD of the fitted structure with respect to the reported de novo model is 0.7 Å and 0.9 Å for cMDFF and ReMDFF respectively, much lower than the 3.7 Å RMSD attained with direct MDFF (Figure 2—figure supplement 3a)
evidence: This is experimental data from the β-galactosidase refinement, presented in Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 3a.

claim: RMSD of the direct MDFF-fitted β-galactosidase structure with respect to the reported de novo model is 3.7 Å.
source: Summarized in Table 1, the fitting results, in terms of quality of fit as well as model quality, are significantly better for cMDFF and ReMDFF than for direct MDFF: (i) RMSD of the fitted structure with respect to the reported de novo model is 0.7 Å and 0.9 Å for cMDFF and ReMDFF respectively, much lower than the 3.7 Å RMSD attained with direct MDFF (Figure 2—figure supplement 3a)
evidence: This is experimental data from the β-galactosidase refinement, presented in Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 3a.

claim: EMRinger scores for cMDFF and ReMDFF of β-galactosidase are 3.16 and 3.45 respectively, higher than the 1.91 obtained for direct MDFF.
source: (ii) EMRinger scores for cMDFF and ReMDFF are 3.16 and 3.45 respectively, higher than the 1.91 obtained for direct MDFF, implying accurate fitting of sidechains into the density
evidence: This is experimental data from the β-galactosidase refinement, presented in Table 1.

claim: Integrated FSC (iFSC2) for β-galactosidase attained higher values of 5.22 Å and 4.66 Å for cMDFF and ReMDFF, respectively, than 2.74 Å for direct MDFF.
source: (iv) integrated FSC (iFSC2, corresponding to the range 3.4–10 Å on the FSC plot obtained as per Appendix 1 - Section 6), considered a more stringent measure of model quality than CC (DiMaio et al., 2015), attained higher values of 5.22 Å and 4.66 Å for cMDFF and ReMDFF, respectively, than 2.74 Å for direct MDFF.
evidence: This is experimental data from the β-galactosidase refinement, presented in Table 1.

claim: GCCs for β-galactosidase improved from an initial value of 0.48 to 0.56, 0.67 and 0.67 for direct, cMDFF, and ReMDFF protocols respectively.
source: (v) GCCs improved from an initial value of 0.48 to 0.56, 0.67 and 0.67 for direct, cMDFF, and ReMDFF protocols respectively.
evidence: This is experimental data from the β-galactosidase refinement, presented in Table 1.

claim: Equilibrium MD simulations of a single structure at room temperature typically exhibit RMSD values relative to the initial structure or the average structure of about 3 Å.
source: In judging the RMSD values to the target model the reader is reminded that equilibrium MD simulations of a single structure at room temperature typically exhibit RMSD values relative to the initial structure or the average structure of about 3 Å; the same is true for β-galactosidase (see Figure 2—figure supplement 6 in Appendix 1 - Section 7).
evidence: This is established knowledge about MD simulations, supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 6.

claim: cMDFF and ReMDFF refinements of TRPV1 produced structures that interpret the 3.4-Å TRPV1 map within an RMSD of 2.4 Å and 2.5 Å from the target de novo model.
source: For example, cMDFF and ReMDFF refinements produced structures that interpret the 3.4-Å TRPV1 map within an RMSD of 2.4 Å and 2.5 Å from the target de novo model, much more accurately than does direct MDFF which converges to structures at an RMSD of 7.9 Å.
evidence: This is experimental data from the TRPV1 refinement.

claim: Direct MDFF of TRPV1 converges to structures at an RMSD of 7.9 Å from the target de novo model.
source: For example, cMDFF and ReMDFF refinements produced structures that interpret the 3.4-Å TRPV1 map within an RMSD of 2.4 Å and 2.5 Å from the target de novo model, much more accurately than does direct MDFF which converges to structures at an RMSD of 7.9 Å.
evidence: This is experimental data from the TRPV1 refinement.

claim: cMDFF and ReMDFF can have a radius of convergence as high as 25 Å in RMSD.
source: However, the TRPV1 fitting results show that cMDFF and ReMDFF can have a radius of convergence as high as 25 Å in RMSD, whereas direct MDFF requires at the outset a well-fitted structure to deliver a satisfactory model.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from TRPV1 refinement where the initial model deviated by 25 Å.

claim: The ReMDFF protocol exhibited the quickest convergence for β-galactosidase, arriving at steady state within 0.1 ns of simulation, whereas cMDFF requires around 0.8 ns.
source: In terms of efficiency, the ReMDFF protocol exhibits the quickest convergence, arriving at steady state within 0.1 ns of simulation, whereas cMDFF requires around 0.8 ns.
evidence: This is experimental data comparing the efficiency of the two methods for β-galactosidase.

claim: The ReMDFF protocol for TRPV1 exhibited the quickest convergence, arriving at steady state within 0.02 ns of simulation, whereas cMDFF required around 0.27 ns.
source: As was observed already for β-galactosidase, the ReMDFF protocol exhibited the quickest convergence, arriving at steady state within 0.02 ns of simulation, whereas cMDFF required around 0.27 ns.
evidence: This is experimental data comparing the efficiency of the two methods for TRPV1.

claim: RMSF values monitored during an MDFF simulation correlate closely with the overall and local resolution of an EM map.
source: Apart from representing the quality of fit, RMSF values monitored during an MDFF simulation correlate closely with the overall and local resolution of an EM map.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data and analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The lower the resolution of the map, the higher the corresponding overall RMSF during MDFF simulations.
source: Generally, the lower the resolution of the map, the higher the corresponding overall RMSF during MDFF simulations. For example, the overall RMSF during MDFF of the 4.5-Å γ-secretase model and map is greater than that of the 3.4-Å model and map which, in turn, is greater than that of the 2.2-Å map and model of β-galactosidase (see RMSF labels on the upper column of Figure 4).
evidence: This is experimental data showing the correlation between RMSF and map resolution, presented in Figure 4.

claim: RMSFs of atoms plotted against local resolutions of the corresponding map regions display linear correlation between the two quantities.
source: In Figure 4 (upper row), RMSFs of atoms plotted against local resolutions of the corresponding map regions display linear correlation between the two quantities.
evidence: This is experimental data showing the correlation between RMSF and local resolution, presented in Figure 4.

claim: RMSF values during MDFF refinement linearly correlate with RMSF during unbiased MD simulations.
source: The physical basis for considering RMSF values of a group of fitted atoms during an MDFF refinement as an indicator of the map resolution follows from the linear correlation of these values with RMSF of the same set of atoms during unbiased MD (Figure 4, bottom row).
evidence: This is experimental data showing the correlation between RMSF during MDFF and unbiased MD, presented in Figure 4.

claim: The flexibility of a molecule during the imaging process contributes to the limiting resolution of the resulting EM density map.
source: Since the flexibility of a molecule during the imaging process contributes to the limiting resolution of the resulting EM density map (Kucukelbir et al., 2014), it is not surprising that overall and local map resolutions correlate with overall and local RMSF values of the best fitted model (Figure 4).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Kucukelbir et al., 2014.

claim: For β-galactosidase, the B-factor corresponding to the minimum RMSF coincides with the one determined by Guinier analysis to provide maximum contrast.
source: Surprisingly, for all the three structures the B-factor corresponding to the minimum RMSF coincides with the one determined by Guinier analysis (Fernández et al., 2008; Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003) to provide maximum contrast.
evidence: This is experimental data showing the agreement between RMSF-based and Guinier analysis-based B-factor determination.

claim: For TRPV1, B-factors determined from the RMSF minima are found to be higher for the soluble regions than for the transmembrane helices, in agreement with those B-factors derived from the Guinier analysis.
source: In fact, for TRPV1, B-factors determined from the RMSF minima are found to be higher for the soluble regions than for the transmembrane helices (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, b vs. c), again, in agreement with those B-factors derived from the Guinier analysis.
evidence: This is experimental data showing the agreement between RMSF-based and Guinier analysis-based B-factor determination for different regions of TRPV1.

claim: The test system carbon monoxide dehydrogenase converges to the known target structure in approximately 0.1 ns simulation time on Amazon Web Services.
source: To prove the feasibility of performing ReMDFF simulations on a cloud platform, we performed ReMDFF for a test system, carbon monoxide dehydrogenase (PDB 1OAO:chain C), on the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) platform. The test system converges to the known target structure in approximately 0.1 ns simulation time.
evidence: This is experimental data from the cloud computing implementation.

claim: cMDFF and ReMDFF offer accurate fitting of atomic-level structures within sub-5 Å EM maps, a feat thus far inaccessible to direct MDFF.
source: cMDFF and ReMDFF, the new variants of MDFF introduced above, offer now accurate fitting of atomic-level structures within sub-5 Å EM maps, a feat thus far inaccessible to direct MDFF.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The radius of convergence of cMDFF and ReMDFF is at least twice that reported for Rosetta refinements of the 20S proteasome.
source: This radius of convergence is at least twice that reported for Rosetta refinements of the 20S proteasome (DiMaio et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a comparison with published results, supported by citation to DiMaio et al., 2015.

claim: ReMDFF simulations converge quickly using a small number of replicas and are thus amenable to cloud computing applications.
source: ReMDFF simulations involving the so-called replica-exchange molecular dynamics converge quickly using a small number of replicas and are thus amenable to cloud computing applications.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing fast convergence and the cloud computing implementation.

claim: The sub-5 Å EM maps have been able to resolve proteins in multiple conformations.
source: The sub-5 Å EM maps have also been able to resolve proteins in multiple conformations (Matthies et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Matthies et al., 2016.

claim: MDFF provides a natural method to model flexible regions by flexibly fitting de novo models constructed for one conformational state into the density of other state(s).
source: MDFF provides a natural method to model flexible regions; de novo models constructed for one conformational state can be flexibley fitted into the density of the other state(s), thus avoiding the arduous task of model construction for all the conformational states for capturing a conformational transition process with cryo-EM.
evidence: This is a proposed application of MDFF based on its capabilities demonstrated in the manuscript.

claim: At high resolutions, VEM features multiple proximal local minima which correspond to recurring spatial patterns within a macromolecule, such as helices aligned in parallel or strands in a β-sheet.
source: In contrast, at the mid-resolution range of 4–6 Å, densities corresponding to the backbones become discernible, and at sub-4 Å resolutions, even sidechains can be resolved. At such high resolutions, VEM now features multiple proximal local minima which correspond to recurring spatial patterns within a macromolecule, such as helices aligned in parallel or strands in a β-sheet.
evidence: This is an inference based on the nature of high-resolution maps and the MDFF potential.

claim: The energy barriers separating local minima in high-resolution maps are typically twice as high as those in the case of low-resolution maps.
source: As shown in Figure 1, the energy barriers separating these local minima are typically twice as high as those in the case of low-resolution maps.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The existence of potential minima in high-resolution maps exposes MDFF to entrapment of the fitted structure within undesired local minima instead of reaching the global minimum of VEM.
source: The existence of such potential minima in high-resolution maps exposes MDFF to a long-known weakness of traditional MD-based algorithms, namely entrapment of the fitted structure within undesired local minima instead of reaching the global minimum of VEM.
evidence: This is an inference based on known limitations of MD algorithms and the characteristics of high-resolution maps.

claim: Direct MDFF yields structurally poor or functionally irrelevant models with high-resolution EM maps.
source: Not unexpectedly, therefore, direct MDFF yields structurally poor or functionally irrelevant models with high-resolution EM maps (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) (DiMaio et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and citation to DiMaio et al., 2015.

claim: In cMDFF, the structure is fitted, in a series of MDFF simulations, to maps of gradually increasing resolution.
source: To mitigate this weakness in direct MDFF, we introduce cMDFF and ReMDFF. In cMDFF, the structure is fitted, in a series of MDFF simulations, to maps of gradually increasing resolution.
evidence: This is a direct description of the cMDFF methodology.

claim: The density-dependent potential derived from the smoothest map features a clear global minimum representing the large-scale structural features of the protein.
source: Illustrated in Figure 1, the density-dependent potential derived from the smoothest map (i.e. the one with the largest σ value) features a clear global minimum representing the large-scale structural features of the protein.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1 and is a key principle of the cMDFF method.

claim: The gradual increase in map resolution over the course of the simulations allows the structure to explore a greater conformational space than in direct MDFF.
source: The gradual increase in map resolution over the course of the simulations allows the structure to explore a greater conformational space than in direct MDFF.
evidence: This is an inference based on the design of the cMDFF method.

claim: In ReMDFF, multiple MDFF simulation replica are run in parallel with each replica fitting a model to a map of a specific resolution.
source: In ReMDFF, the cascade scheme is infused with a greater degree of automation. Multiple MDFF simulation replica are run in parallel with each replica fitting a model to a map of a specific resolution.
evidence: This is a direct description of the ReMDFF methodology.

claim: ReMDFF has advantages over cMDFF both in terms of efficiency and automation as it can take advantage of modern parallel computing hardware.
source: ReMDFF has advantages over cMDFF both in terms of efficiency and automation as it can take advantage of modern parallel computing hardware and the powerful and adaptive replica exchange interface of NAMD (Jiang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on the design of ReMDFF and citation to NAMD capabilities.

claim: Both cMDFF and ReMDFF outperform direct MDFF in quality and speed across a range of high-resolution examples.
source: Nonetheless, as presented in the following, both cMDFF and ReMDFF outperform direct MDFF in quality and speed across a range of high-resolution examples.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The cMDFF- and ReMDFF-refined structures of β-galactosidase not only exhibit good measures of fit, but also improve the clash score and rotamer geometries, relative to the de novo and initial structures.
source: The results show that the cMDFF- and ReMDFF-refined structures not only exhibit good measures of fit, but also improve the clash score and rotamer geometries, relative to the de novo and initial structures, while incurring only a small expense in Ramachandran statistics, bad angles, and Cβ deviations.
evidence: This is experimental data from the β-galactosidase refinement, presented in Table 2.

claim: The poorer the secondary structure of the search model, measured in terms of higher percentages of rotamer and Ramachandran outliers, the worse the local structural statistics of the MDFF/cMDFF/ReMDFF-refined model.
source: Comparison of the three cMDFF refinements starting with three search models of varying structural quality reveal that the poorer the secondary structure of the search model, measured in terms of higher percentages of rotamer and Ramachandran outliers, the worse the local structural statistics of the MDFF/cMDFF/ReMDFF-refined model.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of experimental data from multiple refinements with different starting models.

claim: Large scale map-model validation measures, such as RMSD, GCC, or iFSC values, remain insensitive to local discrepancies in the refined model.
source: Surprisingly, large scale map-model validation measures, such as RMSD, GCC, or iFSC values, remain insensitive to such local discrepancies in the refined model.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of experimental data showing similar global metrics despite different local structural statistics.

claim: The high-precision of sub-5 Å maps demands correct assignment of secondary structure, which determines backbone geometry directly and sidechain conformations indirectly.
source: The high-precision of sub-5 Å maps demands correct assignment of secondary structure, which determines backbone geometry directly and sidechain conformations indirectly.
evidence: This is an inference based on the nature of high-resolution maps and the requirements for accurate modeling.

claim: Moderate- to high-confidence homology models will serve as the most optimal starting point for MDFF refinement.
source: To this end, notwithstanding observed cMDFF improvements of the secondary structure (Table 2 columns 4 vs. 6, and also demonstrated for γ-secretase [Supplementary file 1D]), moderate- to high-confidence homology models will serve as the most optimal starting point, as has been successfully shown for MDFF with low-resolution EM (Chan et al., 2011; Noble et al., 2013; Wickles et al., 2014) and crystallographic data (McGreevy et al., 2014; Li et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a recommendation based on experimental data and citations to previous successful applications.

claim: A search model which deviates from the target by an RMSD of 7–25 Å featuring Ramachandran outliers of ~3%, poor rotamers of 11–38%, overall Molprobity score of ~4 and EMRinger score of ~0.20 can be accurately refined against a sub-5 Å EM map with cMDFF or ReMDFF.
source: Quantitatively speaking, employing the current example (β-galactosidase) and the following one (TRPV1), it is now shown that a search model which deviates from the target by an RMSD of 7–25 Å featuring Ramachandran outliers of ~3%, poor rotamers of 11–38%, overall Molprobity score of ~4 and EMRinger score of ~0.20 can be accurately refined against a sub-5 Å EM map with cMDFF or ReMDFF.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data from β-galactosidase and TRPV1 refinements.

claim: Fitting of the Cβ atoms to the density is crucial for accurate placement of the sidechains.
source: First, it was found that fitting of the Cβ atoms to the density is crucial for accurate placement of the sidechains.
evidence: This is a finding from additional simulations described in Appendix 1 - Section 7.

claim: MDFF placement of the backbone does not guarantee correct sidechain geometries, even with state-of-the-art CHARMM36 force fields.
source: In agreement with prior EMRringer results (Barad et al., 2015), it is confirmed that MDFF placement of the backbone does not guarantee correct sidechain geometries, even with state-of-the-art CHARMM36 (Klauda et al., 2010) force fields.
evidence: This is a finding confirmed by experimental data and in agreement with prior results cited.

claim: MD simulation of the cMDFF-fitted β-galactosidase model revealed that this model is an excellent representation of the most probable structures of the thermodynamic ensemble that characterizes the 3.2 Å map.
source: Second, MD simulation of the cMDFF-fitted β-galactosidase model revealed that this model is indeed an excellent representation of the most probable structures of the thermodynamic ensemble that characterizes the 3.2 Å map.
evidence: This is a finding from additional simulations described in Appendix 1 - Section 7.

claim: Low RMSF values for the fitted structure indicate that the structure has been modeled unambiguously within the map.
source: Low RMSF values for the fitted structure indicate therefore, that (i) the structure has been modeled unambiguously within the map, and (ii) the structure can be regarded as representative of the ensemble underlying the 3.2-Å β-galactosidase map
evidence: This is an inference based on the relationship between RMSF and ensemble diversity.

claim: Per-residue fluctuations about the fitted structure are less than 1 Å, so only marginal backbone and sidechain variations within the ensemble arise.
source: since per-residue fluctuations about the fitted structure (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) are less than 1 Å, only marginal backbone and sidechain variations within the ensemble arise (Singharoy et al., 2013).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1, with citation to Singharoy et al., 2013.

claim: Conformational flexibility can cause heterogeneity in the cryo-EM data, producing local resolutions lower than that of the overall map.
source: Conformational flexibility can cause heterogeneity in the cryo-EM data (Leschziner and Nogales, 2007), producing local resolutions lower than that of the overall map.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Leschziner and Nogales, 2007.

claim: RMSF, together with GCC, LCC, EMRinger, and iFSC, provide a comprehensive set of criteria for evaluating model and map quality on both global and local levels.
source: In broad terms, through the present study we establish that RMSF, together with GCC, LCC, EMRinger (Barad et al., 2015), and iFSC, provide a comprehensive set of criteria for evaluating model and map quality on both global and local levels.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data and analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The added value of RMSF is particularly evident on the local level, where the other measures may not perform as consistently.
source: The added value of RMSF is particularly evident on the local level, where the other measures may not perform as consistently.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of different validation metrics.

claim: EMRinger scoring, when applied to small groups of residues, does not correlate with local resolution.
source: Likewise, EMRinger scoring, when applied to small groups of residues, does not correlate with local resolution (Figure 4—figure supplement 2b), and, therefore, is incapable of distinguishing regions of small number of atoms by local model quality.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2b.

claim: RMSF clearly resolves local resolution, and, thus, resolves the map and model quality even with as few as 100 atoms.
source: In contrast, RMSF clearly resolves local resolution, and, thus, resolves the map and model quality even with as few as 100 atoms.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing RMSF correlation with local resolution.

claim: B-factor sharpening restores lost contrast by resolving the fuzzy features and is a crucial step of map generation that affects map interpretation.
source: B-factor sharpening restores lost contrast by resolving the fuzzy features and, therefore, is a crucial step of map generation that affects map interpretation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about map processing.

claim: For all three structures (β-galactosidase, TRPV1, γ-secretase), the B-factor corresponding to the minimum RMSF coincides with the one determined by Guinier analysis to provide maximum contrast.
source: Surprisingly, for all the three structures the B-factor corresponding to the minimum RMSF coincides with the one determined by Guinier analysis (Fernández et al., 2008; Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003) to provide maximum contrast.
evidence: This is experimental data from analysis of three different systems.

claim: The RMSF analysis of maps with varying B-factor sharpening provides an alternate procedure for the determination of the optimal B-factor.
source: Therefore, the RMSF analysis of maps with varying B-factor sharpening provides an alternate procedure for the determination of the optimal B-factor, which has been traditionally determined by Guinier analysis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing agreement between RMSF-based and Guinier analysis-based B-factor determination.

claim: The maps that produce the model with the lowest RMSF during fitting represent the density envelopes where atoms can be positioned with the least uncertainty at the given experimental resolutions.
source: Following this argument, the maps in Figure 5, Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Figure 5—figure supplement 2 that produce the model with the lowest RMSF during fitting represent the density envelopes where atoms can be positioned with the least uncertainty at the given experimental resolutions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the relationship between RMSF and map quality.

evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of model quality metrics for sharpened vs. unsharpened maps.

claim: The maximum EMRinger score is attained for the same B-factor that produces the minimum RMSF.
source: Indeed, as further illustrated in Figure 5a, Figure 5—figure supplement 3b, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1, the maximum EMRinger score is attained for the same B-factor that produces the minimum RMSF.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in multiple figures.

claim: Correlation of the RMSF of the fitted structure with that from an unbiased MD of the system is preserved for the B-factor sharpened map.

evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5b and Figure 5—figure supplement 2b.
